pages.title: Heat Exchanger Terminal
pages.text: The controller. Shows both channels, their fluids, their temperatures and the rate at which heat is moving between them.$(br2)It is also where assembly errors are reported.

pages.title: Heat Exchanger Casing
pages.text: Frame and walls. Every edge and corner has to be casing.

pages.title: Condenser Channel
pages.text: The hot side. Carries the fluid that is giving up heat, normally turbine exhaust on its way back to being water.$(br2)Channels form a pipe: each one connects to exactly two neighbours, and the run has to start at one Fluid Port and end at another.

pages.title: Evaporator Channel
pages.text: The cold side. Carries the fluid that is taking heat up.$(br2)Same rules as the condenser: exactly two connections per block, port at each end. The two channel types never connect to each other, which is what keeps the loops separate.

pages.title: Fluid Port
pages.text: Exactly four are required: two on the condenser run and two on the evaporator run.$(br2)Each port picks up its channel type from whichever channel it touches, and toggles between $(thing)Inlet$() and $(thing)Outlet$() in its interface.

pages.title: Computer Port
pages.text: Exposes both channels to Lua scripting with a computer mod such as $(thing)CC: Tweaked$().

pages.title: Heat Exchanger Glass
pages.text: Wall only, never frame. Lets you see the channel layout inside, which is worth it while you are still getting the connections right.
